name: Reactance
statement: When a rule or a message threatens a freedom people believe they hold, they push back to restore it, which can make the discouraged option more appealing.
meaning: Reactance is a motivational state rather than a preference. Brehm's claim is that people hold beliefs about which behaviours are open to them, and that a threat to one of those behaviours creates pressure to reassert it. Steindl and colleagues, summarising the 1966 book, put the size of the reaction down to two things: how important the threatened freedom is, and how large the threat looks. Three things travel under the name and they come apart. The state is the aroused reaction to one particular threat. The trait is a standing disposition to react that way, measured by questionnaire. The boomerang effect is an outcome, where an audience moves away from what a message advocated. A message can raise the state without producing the outcome, and most of the argument about reactance sits in that gap.

origin.note: Brehm set out the theory in a book, A Theory of Psychological Reactance. Experiments testing it appeared the same year, one of them by Brehm with Lloyd Stires, John Sensenig and Janet Shaban on the attractiveness of an eliminated choice alternative.

evidence: The first experiments took an option away and measured what happened to its appeal. Brehm, Stires, Sensenig and Shaban tested the attractiveness of an eliminated choice alternative. Hammock and Brehm tested the same thing when the freedom to choose was removed by another person. Both appeared in 1966, and neither those papers nor Brehm's book could be obtained for this entry, so nothing is taken from them beyond their titles and their records at Crossref. Reactance was then treated for decades as a state that could not be measured directly. Dillard and Shen changed that in 2005 by treating it as an amalgam of anger and negative cognitions, captured with rating scales and thought-listing. In two studies, one advocating flossing and one urging students to drink less, a composite index of anger and negative cognitions fully mediated the effects of threat to freedom and trait reactance on attitude and intention. Rains later pooled the literature and reported that this intertwined model, with reactance as a latent factor and anger and counterarguments as its indicators, fitted better than the alternatives. His paper is paywalled, and both its scope and its coefficients are quoted here from Reynolds-Tylus: 20 studies and 4,942 participants, loadings of 0.62 for anger against 0.52 for negative cognitions, correlations with attitude of 0.20 and 0.16, and a correlation between anger and negative cognitions of 0.31. Trait reactance is measured separately, usually with the Hong Psychological Reactance Scale. Shen and Dillard tested its 11-item version on three samples of 188, 200 and 233 people and found four first-order factors that could be treated as one factor at the second order.

replication.headline: Controlling language reliably raises anger and counterarguing, and the reversal it is supposed to cause often fails to arrive.
replication.detail: Li and Shi pooled 28 articles, 33 studies and 146 effect sizes published between 2005 and 2024. High freedom-threatening language beat low freedom-threatening language on reactance at r = .20, 95% CI [.16, .23], across 53 effects, with anger at r = .21 and negative cognitions at r = .17. Gain against loss framing did nothing, r = -.02 across 12 effects, 95% CI [-.08, .05]. Reactance in turn tracked weaker persuasion, anger at r = -.23 and negative cognitions at r = -.18, which is dampening rather than reversal. A second meta-analysis, by Ma, Ma, Kalny and Walter across 35 studies and 10,658 people, reports findings that align with the theory alongside heterogeneity between studies. It is paywalled and none of its effect sizes are quoted here. The mandate studies from 2020 onward split. Albarracin, Jung, Song, Tan and Fishman ran four US studies in which requiring vaccination raised intentions rather than lowering them. A survey of 299 people gave d = 0.64, and a preregistered study of 606 recruited to census quotas gave d = 0.10, F(1, 593) = 6.24, p = .01. Trait reactance was measured in the third and fourth studies only, and it never marked out the people who resisted. Sprengholz, Betsch and Bohm found movement the other way in a German sample of 973 and a preregistered US study that recruited 1,701 and analysed 1,394. A mandate raised reactance among people whose baseline intention to vaccinate was low, interaction b = -0.72, 95% CI [-0.82, -0.61], and scarce supply raised it among those whose intention was high, b = 0.57, 95% CI [0.46, 0.67]. Reactance in turn predicted intentions to act against the restriction. Verpaalen and colleagues followed a Dutch panel through a vaccination programme, 1,411 at the first wave and 865 with data at all three. Reactance at the first wave predicted lower intention at the second, printed as B = -0.07, a standardised coefficient of -.06 and an interval of -0.14 to -0.01. That path was no longer reliable among the 865, and controlling for intention, reactance did not predict whether anyone got vaccinated.

study.cite: Li, Z., & Shi, J. (2026). Message effects on psychological reactance: meta-analyses. Human Communication Research, 52(1), 38-52.

limits: The pooled figures come from studies of message wording, mostly on health topics and mostly with US samples. They describe what a forceful sentence does to a questionnaire, not what a law does to behaviour. Tests outside that literature are small, and Elmore, Oyserman, Smith and Novin's classroom work on how pupils read difficulty ran on 93 students without reactance conditions and 181 with them. The standard trait measure is unsettled. Waris and colleagues tested 12 previously published factor solutions of the Hong scale in two Finnish samples of 624 and 518 people, found a single factor fitted best in both confirmatory and exploratory analyses, and reported that this factor accounted for about 40% of total variance. A shortened version fitted better than the full scale, and they concluded the scale could use improvement. Rosenberg and Siegel divide the field into five overlapping waves rather than one accumulating literature, ending in a return to motivation, and their 2025 introduction to a nine-article special issue makes the same division. Their 2018 review was read here in abstract only. Searches of Crossref and Europe PMC on 17 August 2026, pairing reactance with many-labs, multi-laboratory, registered-replication and Psychological Science Accelerator terms, turned up no multi-laboratory replication of a reactance experiment.
misreadings: Reactance is not general contrariness. It is tied to a specific freedom the person believed they held, and a message that threatens nothing arouses none of it. A high score on the Hong scale is not a measure of how much reactance somebody felt on a given occasion. It is a trait questionnaire, and in the two studies of Albarracin and colleagues that measured it, it did not identify who resisted a mandate. Where it interacted with the manipulation at all, the more reactant participants formed the stronger intentions to vaccinate. Raised anger and counterarguing are also not a boomerang. The meta-analytic path from reactance to persuasion is negative, meaning the message works less well rather than backwards, and the outcome has its own entry at the boomerang effect, no. 509. The Romeo and Juliet effect is often produced as reactance in the wild. Sinclair, Hood and Wright followed 396 people for three to four months on Driscoll, Davis and Lipetz's original measures and could not find it: interference and disapproval went with poorer relationships, not better ones. The 'backfire effect' argued over in the misinformation literature is a separate phenomenon about how people update factual beliefs, and it is covered at no. 157.
